_comment: What kind of paper each masthead is, so the clipping list can be filtered and arranged by it. Four axes, one value each per paper, so a paper is in exactly one bucket per axis and nested filters cannot contradict each other. THIS FILE SHIPS WITH THE APP AND IS NEVER WRITTEN TO. The user's own corrections go to categories.json in the app-data folder as a list of changed fields, so an update brings new papers in without wiping what they have edited. 'checked' says how sure this is: verified = confirmed against a published source; known = general knowledge, high confidence; unsure = the paper could not be confirmed at all, and is the first thing the user should correct.

reach.label: Reach
reach.help: How far the paper travels. Northern Railway's belt is Delhi, UP, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Punjab, Himachal and Jammu & Kashmir, so 'Regional' means that belt.

language.label: Language
language.help: The language the paper is printed in.

stature.label: Size
stature.help: How big the publication is, as a stand-in for how much a story in it matters. Judged within the belt: The Tribune is not a national heavyweight, but in Chandigarh it is the paper that counts.

medium.label: Medium
medium.help: Not everything in a morning's clippings is a newspaper. Channels, websites and social posts arrive in the same documents and must not be forced into a newspaper category.

papers.name: Dainik Jagran
papers.note: India's most-read Hindi daily, around 37 editions across the Hindi belt.

papers.name: Amar Ujala
papers.note: 22 editions in six states; the default Hindi paper of UP and Uttarakhand.

papers.name: Hindustan
papers.note: HT Media's Hindi daily; dominant in UP, Bihar, Uttarakhand and Delhi.

papers.name: Dainik Bhaskar
papers.note: One of the two largest Hindi dailies in the country.

papers.name: Punjab Kesari
papers.note: The Hind Samachar group's Hindi flagship across Punjab, Haryana, Himachal, Delhi and Jammu.

papers.name: Navbharat Times
papers.note: The Times group's Hindi daily; a Delhi and NCR heavyweight.

papers.name: Rashtriya Sahara
papers.note: Sahara group; Delhi, Lucknow, Kanpur, Gorakhpur, Varanasi and Dehradun editions.

papers.name: Jansatta
papers.note: The Indian Express group's Hindi daily. A small print run, but read by officials and editors.

papers.name: Nai Duniya
papers.note: Jagran-owned; strong in Madhya Pradesh, thinner in the Northern Railway belt.

papers.name: Dainik Savera
papers.note: Punjab's big Hindi challenger since 2011: 23 editions in six states. Called Major because of what it is inside Punjab; the circulation figure behind that is the publisher's own.

papers.name: Amrit Vichar
papers.note: Bareilly, Lucknow, Moradabad, Haldwani, Ayodhya and Kanpur editions.

papers.name: Dainik Tribune
papers.note: The Tribune Trust's Hindi edition from Chandigarh.

papers.name: Aaj
papers.note: Historic Varanasi daily, founded 1920, still published across eastern UP.

papers.name: Virat Vaibhav
papers.note: Delhi Hindi daily since 2005, with Jaipur and Jodhpur editions.

papers.name: Swatantra Bharat
papers.note: Lucknow Hindi daily started on 15 August 1947. A name with history, a small paper now.

papers.name: Hindi Milap
papers.note: Worth a look: the Milap group split after Partition. Hyderabad's Hindi Milap is Hindi; Delhi's Daily Milap is Urdu. A Delhi clipping saying only Milap is more likely the Urdu one.

papers.name: Rashtriya Swaroop
papers.note: A Delhi Hindi daily on e-paper listings; no circulation figure found.

papers.name: Uttar Kesari
papers.note: Only ever seen as a Moradabad city clipping. Could not be confirmed as an independent title.

papers.name: Samarth Bandhu
papers.note: Only ever seen as a Chandigarh edition in Ambala Division files.

papers.name: Rashtriya News Network
papers.note: Only ever seen in Ambala Division files.

papers.name: Surodhay Bharat
papers.note: Only ever seen in Jammu Division files.

papers.name: Samachar Post
papers.note: Only ever seen in Jammu Division files.

papers.name: Dainik Ujala
papers.note: Does not appear in any sample clipping. May be a name typed once.

papers.name: Amar Bharti
papers.note: Does not appear in any sample clipping. May be a name typed once.

papers.name: The Times of India
papers.note: The largest-circulation English broadsheet there is; Delhi and Chandigarh editions appear here.

papers.name: Hindustan Times
papers.note: Delhi's leading English daily; the Chandigarh edition turns up in Ambala files.

papers.name: The Indian Express
papers.note: National English daily with a real Chandigarh presence and a habit of scrutinising the railways.

papers.name: The Hindu
papers.note: The national paper of record. Thin in the north, but it sets the agenda.

papers.name: The Economic Times
papers.note: India's dominant business daily.

papers.name: Business Standard
papers.note: A serious national business daily, much smaller than the Economic Times.

papers.name: The Tribune
papers.note: The Chandigarh institution, and the English paper of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal.

papers.name: The Statesman
papers.note: An old Kolkata and Delhi title; a prestigious name with a modest reach today.

papers.name: The Pioneer
papers.note: Delhi and Lucknow English daily; small, but read inside government.

papers.name: Millennium Post
papers.note: Delhi and NCR English daily launched in 2012.

papers.name: Mail Today
papers.note: The India Today and Daily Mail Delhi compact. The print edition is believed to have stopped, and it appears in no sample clipping.

papers.name: Daily Excelsior
papers.note: The most-read English daily of Jammu, and the first thing a Jammu desk looks at.

papers.name: Kashmir Times
papers.note: A long-standing Jammu and Srinagar English daily.

papers.name: Early Times
papers.note: Jammu English daily since 2002, with Srinagar, Leh and Udhampur editions.

papers.name: State Times
papers.note: Jammu English daily covering the administration day to day.

papers.name: Journey Line
papers.note: English daily published from Jammu city.

papers.name: Ajit
papers.note: The largest-circulation Punjabi daily, from Jalandhar.

papers.name: Jag Bani
papers.note: The Hind Samachar group's Punjabi daily, Punjab Kesari's sister paper.

papers.name: Punjabi Tribune
papers.note: The Tribune Trust's Punjabi edition; the serious Punjabi read.

papers.name: Rozana Spokesman
papers.note: Jalandhar, launched 1993; among the larger Punjabi dailies.

papers.name: Charhdikala
papers.note: Patiala Punjabi daily since 1977, strong on Sikh affairs.

papers.name: Daily Post
papers.note: Chandigarh broadsheet since 2011. It is published in Punjabi and Hindi, so this one value cannot be right for every edition.

papers.name: Punjabi Jagran
papers.note: Jagran Prakashan's Punjabi daily from Jalandhar. Until now it was being counted as Dainik Jagran, so Punjabi clippings were showing up as Hindi ones.

papers.name: Ajit Samachar
papers.note: The Ajit group's Hindi daily from Jalandhar. A different paper from the Punjabi Ajit.

papers.name: Haribhoomi
papers.note: Since 1996. The Rohtak and Delhi editions are the ones that reach this belt.

papers.name: Jagmarg
papers.note: Chandigarh Hindi daily circulating in Punjab and Haryana.

papers.name: News Times Ludhiana
papers.note: Seen once, in a Firozpur Division file. Language not confirmed.

papers.name: Prath Kiran
papers.note: Seen once, as a Bijnor city clipping.

papers.name: Bedaak Kesari
papers.note: Seen once, as a Najibabad city clipping.

papers.name: Uturn
papers.note: Seen once, from Amritsar. Language not confirmed.

papers.name: Aaj Tak
papers.note: A news channel, not a paper. Listed so it is never counted as the Varanasi daily Aaj.

papers.name: ABP News
papers.note: A news channel, not a paper.

papers.name: Times Now
papers.note: A news channel, not a paper. Listed so it is never counted as The Times of India.

papers.name: Babushahi.com
papers.note: A Punjab news website.

papers.name: Facebook
papers.note: Social media, not a publication.

papers.name: Twitter
papers.note: Social media, not a publication. Also written as X.

papers.name: Instagram
papers.note: Social media, not a publication.

papers.name: YouTube
papers.note: Social media, not a publication.
